editorial:
Imagine being a teen who lives for loud guitars and big crowds, but then you start hearing a voice that tells you to do the one thing you hate: run. That is exactly what happens here. You get to follow a kid who is totally obsessed with becoming a rock star, but his life takes a weird turn when this mysterious voice pushes him to train for a full marathon. The vibe is really sweet and hopeful, mixing the energy of a garage band with the grit of long-distance running. It is a great look at how someone can find strength in places they never expected.

What really works is the acting; the lead feels like a real teenager and not some polished Hollywood version. The pacing is steady, though a few training scenes feel a bit long. If you like stories about overcoming the odds, you will love this. You should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to get the best sound for the music scenes. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move because the colors are just stunning.
endingExplained: In the final race, you find out the mysterious voice was actually the spirit of his grandfather, who was a runner but never got to finish his own big race. As the teen crosses the finish line, the voice finally goes quiet because its mission is done. He realizes that the discipline from running actually makes him a better musician. He ends the movie playing a huge show, finally balancing his love for music and fitness.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves underdog stories and great music.
